newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bank task force to probe competition issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bank task force to probe competition issues.

text.p: A task force examining regulation and competition in the Canadian financial services industry said on Friday it wanted to probe rules that restrict foreign competition, mergers and holding companies.

The task force aims to develop a framework that should "reflect judgments on, for example, the trade-off between prudential regulation and freedom of competition," the panel said in a discussion paper released today.
"Questions include whether the sector is now so international that we can accept international competition as a sufficient discipline in the Canadian domestic market," the report said.

The task force under Toronto lawyer James Baillie was expected to make recommendations to the government by September 1998. The panel was set up after the banking industry complained that government proposals in 1996 for financial services reform did not address fundamental issues.
Current legislation prevents any one investor from owning more than 10 percent of Canada's big banks, effectively banning takeovers.
The task force said it would re-examine these rules in light of domestic and international competition, the task force said.

The panel also said it would pay close attention to the entry of foreign banks into Canada. New rules governing foreign-owned banks would allow them to operate through branches rather than subsidiaries when they come into effect later this year.
"The task force notes these developments and seeks comment as to whether they adequately deal with the issue of foreign bank entry," the discussion paper said.
The task force will also look at whether foreign subsidiaries need to comply with Canadian deposit insurance requirements.
The panel will also be examining whether rules that discourage mergers between regulated financial institutions should be changed.

The task force will try to outline the appropriate regulatory structure to deal with financial institutions that do business in Canada without establishing a physical presence in the country. Foreign institutions using electronics or direct mail have a growing presence in Canada.
The panel will also look at existing regulations governing second-tier financial institutions to see if the rules are too overbearing.
"We ask whether greater reliance might be placed on private sector initiatives, including self-regulatory organizations and credit rating agencies," the report said.
The task force will also look at the banks' accountability to the public, the availabililty of loans and the ability of the financial services sector to create and maintain jobs in Canada.
